system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:

    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the

answer.rationale: The two deteriorating metrics are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and the inherited record contains two convergent, independently consolidated results pointing at the funnel itself: memory_86 (shortening onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value across self-serve) and memory_31 (cutting required signup fields produced a durable SMB activation lift). Fixing the funnel is the direction most plausibly tied to sustainable qualified revenue, because it compounds for every later cohort rather than buying a one-time cohort. I am deliberately not taking the competitor bait with promotional_pricing: memory_73 reports a genuine +31% conversion and +18% revenue, but with a 12-point later-cycle retention loss under an unchanged support model, which is close to the definition of unsustainable revenue and would also structurally concede on price against a competitor whose entry pricing we cannot durably undercut. activation_messaging (memory_91) is the strongest runner-up but its record is stated only in engagement and 'first meaningful action' terms with no revenue or retention linkage, so it is the weaker single-slot bet. referral_incentive (memory_57) is clean but keyed to established customers and does not touch the two declining metrics; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment that is not the one under attack. I spend both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_31 because they are the memories my chosen action actually rests on, and both carry a specific failure mode worth checking before commit: whether the measured lift was activation-only or carried through to qualified revenue, and whether the removed signup fields were qualification fields. If they were, 'simplification' may have improved activation while degrading lead quality downstream, which would invert the decision. I also want to see whether those results came from a pre-competitor pricing environment and from segments comparable to the price-sensitive SMB accounts we are now losing. Caveats I am holding rather than resolving: memory_31's 'durable' is unverified as to horizon, memory_86 does not report retention at all, and all six memories are consolidated summaries whose original effect sizes and controls I cannot see. Standard experiment scale with explicit guardrails on lead quality and downstream retention, not a broad rollout, so that a false positive on activation cannot silently propagate into the pipeline.
